why_how.text: Approaching a left turn, signal three to five seconds in advance, slow gradually while checking the rearview mirror to confirm the driver behind understood, make sure no bicyclist or vehicle behind is trying to pass on your left, and on a multilane road be in the left lane well ahead of the turn without moving suddenly from the right lane.

At the left turn itself, wait until no vehicles are oncoming, position the vehicle within one foot of the centerline when safe, and keep the wheels straight until you actually turn so a rear end hit will not push you into oncoming traffic.
A left turn sets up within one foot of the centerline, whereas a right turn sets up about three feet from the right edge of the road.
Any oncoming vehicle or bicyclist has the right-of-way over a left turning driver, and pedestrians crossing the street you are turning into must also be yielded to.
Once the road is clear, complete the left turn at a proper speed keeping to the right of the center line, then check the rearview mirror and center the vehicle in its lane.
Before a left turn the driver searches the intersection to the right, the front and the left, and enters the new street just to the right of its center line.
A left turn search runs right, front, left, while a right turn search runs left, front, right and then quickly left again.

On the approach to a right turn keep the vehicle roughly three feet from the road's right edge, never swing out to the left first, and put the signal on three to five seconds ahead while slowing and checking the mirror.

Before a right turn the driver searches the intersection left, front, right and then quickly left again, stays alert for bicyclists or pedestrians on the right side, must yield to any of them, and keeps close to the right side of the lane while turning.
When turning into a street with more than one lane in your direction, turn into the nearest lane, and then follow the multilane rule of driving on the right unless passing or turning.

why_how.text: Passing the written test does not by itself issue a learner's permit; the permit is issued only after every other requirement is met and every required document is provided.
Most motor vehicle crashes are caused by the actions or errors of the driver, and any motorist can drive safely through care, courtesy and caution and by modeling proper behavior.
A new permit holder should begin practicing in an empty parking lot or on lightly traveled roads to build basic car control before moving to busier roads as skills improve.
When a slow driver has traffic piling up behind, the law requires that driver to move to the roadside once it is safe and let the vehicles behind go past.

Hands belong on the steering wheel at the nine and three or the eight and four clock positions, with hand over hand steering used for turns, while practicing left and right turns, smooth braking and controlled starts and stops.

Driver readiness before moving means adjusting the seat, adjusting all mirrors, testing the foot and parking brakes, adjusting and fastening the safety belt, locking the doors and turning on the headlights.

title.text: Pull over when traffic backs up

lines.text: Pull over when traffic backs up

narration.text: When a slow driver has traffic piling up behind, the law requires that driver to move to the roadside once it is safe and let the vehicles behind go past. Hands belong on the steering wheel at the nine and three or the eight and four clock positions, with hand over hand steering used for turns, while practicing left and right turns, smooth braking and controlled starts and stops. Driver readiness before moving means adjusting the seat, adjusting all mirrors, testing the foot and parking brakes, adjusting and fastening the safety belt, locking the doors and turning on the headlights.
